messages.subject: genetic mapping
parts:
Hi everybody,

I have four BC1S3 populations and SNP-Data to map them. I allready mapped my populations with another program but that program gives me a map with big gaps as it isnt able to compute a BC1S3 Population.
I tried now to make a new map with R/qtl and I tried to do like it was advised by the manuals, but when I try to run

heb_25_3.bc1s3<-read.cross("csv", file="/home/R/Matrix_Fam3_R_2.csv",genotypes=c("AA","BB"),na.strings="-", sep=";",dec=",",alleles = c("A","B"))

or any other version to read in my data, R  begins to compute but never stops as it just gives me something like this as an result:

 --Read the following data:
     62  individuals
     7865  markers
     1  phenotypes
 --Estimating genetic map

but no cross type comes up. I tried to give it some more time as I have about 7800 markers, but even after 1h it still wasnt ready.
So now I do not know what kind of problem it is exactly and how to handle it.

I attached the data sheet of one of my populations, maybe I got something wrong there?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] genetic mapping
parts:
Use estimate.map=FALSE in the call to read.cross() so that it's not trying to estimate the map as the data are read in.
Also use crosstype="bcsft", BC.gen=1, F.gen=3.

And I'd recommend including your initial map from that other program within the csv file.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] genetic mapping
parts:
There's a bug in read.cross for crosstype="bcsft".

For now, leave off the crosstype, BC.gen, and F.gen

heb_25_3.bc1s3<-read.cross("csv", file="/home/franziska/Dokumente/MasterBio/Masterarbeit/Daten/Quant_Daten/R/Matrix_Fam3_R_2.csv",sep=";",genotypes=c("AA","BB"),na.strings="-",alleles = c("A","B"),estimate.map=FALSE)

You could then use convert2bcsft() to convert to the bcsft cross type, except your data have just AA and BB genotypes, which is inconsistent with this being a BC1F3 cross.

You could use the following, but the lack of AB genotypes is a problem.

heb_25_3.bc1s3<-read.cross("csv", file="/home/franziska/Dokumente/MasterBio/Masterarbeit/Daten/Quant_Daten/R/Matrix_Fam3_R_2.csv",sep=";",genotypes=c("AA","AB","BB"),na.strings="-",alleles = c("A","B"),estimate.map=FALSE)
heb_25_3.bc1s3 <- convert2bcsft(heb_25_3.bc1s3, BC.gen=1, F.gen=3, estimate.map=FALSE)

karl
